recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-39038 unless a future work-group decision chooses to turn additional cross-resource or payload-level SubscriptionStatus guidance into computable profile-specific constraints.
issue_request: FHIR-39038 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 FHIR-I change request asking for the SubscriptionStatus notification-type rules, especially notificationEvent presence or absence requirements based on type, to be represented as programmatically readable resource constraints where feasible.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 33515587d4c23bf276f2dd950e08dba72c7879f4 on 2023-02-22. That commit added sst-1 and sst-2 invariants to source/subscriptionstatus/structuredefinition-SubscriptionStatus.xml and changed the query-status narrative so notificationEvent is no longer prohibited, matching the constraint scope that can be enforced from the SubscriptionStatus instance alone.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists subscriptionstatus=SubscriptionStatus as an active resource, so the inspected SubscriptionStatus source is in current build scope. Current notes still say event-notification and query-event require notificationEvent, query-status requires status and may contain recent notifications, and handshake/heartbeat may include historical events. Broader payload-level and delivery-guarantee rules depend on Subscription or SubscriptionTopic context and remain narrative guidance. FHIR-I WGM minutes record the Persuasive with Modification 7-0-1 motion, and related FHIR-39040 has already been audited on the combined branch without changing this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current StructureDefinition already carries sst-1 requiring notificationEvent for event-notification or query-event, and sst-2 requiring status for query-status; the current narrative is consistent with those computable invariants and does not support adding broader cross-resource constraints.
